clue.text: Reliable school accepts reproach for the most part

indicators.note: the school abbreviation takes another piece inside it, as a container accepts contents
most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to taunt someone is to reproach or jeer at them

explanation.surface: A dependable school mostly puts up with criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproach' looks like the definition beside 'Reliable', but it is fodder: only 'Reliable' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch supporter is loyal and dependable, so the adjective is a synonym of reliable.

clue.text: The French component in a metal aeroplane part

indicators.note: the French article is a component placed in the metal word

parts.note: iron is a metal
le is the French masculine for the

explanation.surface: French workers make a component of a metal plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a metal' looks like one piece; the A stands alone, ahead of the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged flap on an aircraft's wing used to control roll.

clue.text: With end of evening, personal ' special thing to put on?

annotationWithheld.why: With end of evening, personal special thing to put on: NIGHT + G + OWN needs 'end of evening' to give both NIGHT and G, one phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: With end of evening, personal ' special thing to put on?

clue.text: Ape's soon him with evolution?

indicators.note: evolution suggests change over time, so the letters develop into a new order

parts.note: the word with its possessive s supplies the letters A, P, E, S

explanation.surface: An ape will soon turn into a man through evolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearranging APESSOONHIM gives the species that evolved from apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Humankind is the species descended from ape-like ancestors through evolution, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: A capital orchestra took off hopeless performer

parts.note: the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra, an orchestra of the capital
ran, as in fled or bolted, means took off

explanation.surface: A London orchestra fled from a performer with no chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The LSO, the London Symphony Orchestra, is the orchestra of Britain's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a competitor who finishes unplaced, hence a performer with no hope of winning.

clue.text: Saint could shortly appear thus as one near crib

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint, as the clue's 'shortly' hints

explanation.surface: A saint in short might be seen this way beside the manger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could shortly appear thus' tells you Saint is abbreviated. The crib is the Nativity manger, beside which an ass traditionally stands.
explanation.definitionFit: In Nativity scenes a donkey stands beside the manger where the infant lies.

clue.text: Leaders of soldiers will express army rage to do this?

definitions.text: Leaders of soldiers will express army rage to do this?

indicators.note: the leading letters of each following word are taken in turn

explanation.surface: Commanders of troops voice the army's anger by cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: soldiers venting rage are known for this.
explanation.definitionFit: Angry soldiers are proverbially foul-mouthed, so cursing is what they would do to vent fury.

clue.text: Instrument featured in new air for Italian consumption

indicators.note: the instrument is featured inside the rearranged letters
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters beside it

parts.note: a viol is an early stringed instrument

explanation.surface: An instrument plays a fresh tune for Italian listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' tempts towards a definition, but 'Italian consumption' defines: something Italians eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli is an Italian pasta dish, food eaten in Italy.

clue.text: They're saved from time bomb in loch

indicators.note: the time and bomb pieces are placed in the loch's name

parts.note: Ness is the Scottish loch famed for its monster
egg is old RAF slang for a bomb

explanation.surface: Savings are rescued from a timed bomb in a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link here. Loch Ness is a lake in Scotland; airmen called bombs eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nest eggs are sums of money put by for the future, i.e. savings.

clue.text: More than one sport dances around lame

indicators.note: the word for dances is placed around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: balls are formal dances
game is an old word for a lame or crippled leg, as in a game leg

explanation.surface: Several sports involve dancing round someone limping.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'game leg' is a lame one, the sense used here.
explanation.definitionFit: Football, tennis and cricket are each played with a ball, so the plural names several such sports.

clue.text: English prayers for protecting house?

parts.note: Aves are Ave Marias, the Hail Mary prayers

explanation.surface: English people pray for their home to be kept safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: eaves overhang the walls and shield a house from rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The overhanging edges of a roof keep rain off the walls, so they are a part of a building that shelters it.

clue.text: Demon's getting right into a violent outburst

indicators.note: one piece gets into the other, so it is placed inside it
one piece gets into the other, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: a fit is a sudden violent outburst, as of temper

explanation.surface: A demon goes right into a frenzy of rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Demon's' stands for 'has' or 'is' and links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An afrit is an evil spirit in Arabian mythology, a kind of fiend.

clue.text: Very good attitude to put over? Exactly

parts.note: super is a colloquial word for very good
a pose is a bodily attitude or posture

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fine attitude should be conveyed, and is told yes, precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is split across a question mark: to superpose is to place one thing over another so that they coincide exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry, figures are laid one on another so all their parts coincide, which is placing something over another precisely.

clue.text: Greatly increase professional's cost of living?

parts.note: pro is short for professional
read playfully, the rate charged for life, living expressed as life and cost as rate

explanation.surface: The professional's living costs soar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cost of living' is read word by word: living is LIFE, cost is RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To proliferate is to multiply rapidly in number.

clue.text: In Scotland, notable male's vowing to be tough

parts.note: unco is a Scots word meaning remarkable or notable
M is the abbreviation for male
promising means vowing or pledging

explanation.surface: A remarkable Scottish man swears he will be hard.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCO is Scots dialect for remarkable or extraordinary; the clue flags it with 'In Scotland'.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncompromising person refuses to yield, so being so means being hard and unbending.

clue.text: Used blades to get fish cold all round

indicators.note: the word for cold goes all round the fish

parts.note: iced means chilled, cold
skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone used knives to have a fish chilled through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used blades' sounds like cutting; the blades are those of skates.
explanation.definitionFit: Skates have metal runners called blades, so gliding on them over a frozen surface is using blades.

clue.text: Old car firm in nasty Basque dispute

indicators.note: the car firm sits in the middle of the rearranged letters
nasty suggests the word is mangled and its letters reordered

parts.note: BL was British Leyland, a former British car maker

explanation.surface: A defunct motor company is caught up in an ugly Basque row.
explanation.walkthrough: British Leyland was a UK car maker of the 1970s, long gone, hence 'Old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A squabble is a petty quarrel, an argument over something minor.

clue.text: College to deceive, sadly, about name which prosecution wants?

parts.note: Queens' at Cambridge and Queen's at Oxford are colleges

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed about the other piece, surrounding it
sadly signals that the letters are in a sorry, disordered state and must be rearranged

parts.note: the verb deceive, with 'to' marking the infinitive, supplies the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Someone at college plots, regrettably, to mislead over a name the prosecutor is after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges DECEIVE to EVIDCEE and 'about' puts it round N, giving EVIDENCE. In Britain, a criminal who 'turns Queen's evidence' testifies against accomplices.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given against fellow accused by an accomplice is just what a prosecuting lawyer hopes to obtain.

clue.text: Ask, in French, to get some paper

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a quire is a set quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: Asking in French for some paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To enquire is to seek information by putting a question.

clue.text: Gorge a dairy product

definitions.meaning: a gorge is a steep narrow valley; there is a famous one in Somerset, England
a hard cheese originally from that Somerset village

explanation.surface: Stuffing yourself with dairy food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a verb, eat greedily; it is the noun for a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: The ravine in Somerset and the cheese named after the village beside it share one name.

clue.text: Momentarily brilliant, knowing about tree

indicators.note: the word for knowing goes about the tree, enclosing it

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Briefly dazzling, someone wise about trees.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY as an adjective is British slang for streetwise, knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flashy is showy, glittering for a moment like a flash of light, without lasting substance.

clue.text: A Conservative monarch is constraining English church to give assent

parts.note: Qu. is an abbreviation for queen, a monarch

indicators.note: the word is holds the next piece inside it, constraining it

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Tory queen hems in the English church to secure its agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constraining' puts E inside IS, giving IES.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquiesce is to accept or agree to something without protest, a form of consent.

clue.text: Useless in English and another school subject …

parts.note: PT is physical training, another subject besides English

explanation.surface: Someone is hopeless at English and another subject too.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, was the British school name for gym lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or incompetent, of no use at a task.

clue.text: Some number in vessel get ready to pray

indicators.note: the number abbreviation is placed in the word for the vessel

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge, a kind of vessel

explanation.surface: A few people aboard a boat prepare for prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: KEEL here is the old word for a coal barge, not the ship's spine.
explanation.definitionFit: People go down on their knees before praying, so this is preparing for prayer.

clue.text: Coarse cloth that will do for horses, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for the horses is said aloud, not written

parts.note: bays are reddish-brown horses

explanation.surface: Some rough fabric will suit the horses, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIZE is the green felt-like cloth on snooker and card tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Baize is a coarse woollen fabric, usually green, used to cover tables.

clue.text: Minimum variations in wavelength?

parts.note: read as physics about radiation, but 'wave length' means the reach of the sea's waves, and the tides with the smallest rise and fall

explanation.surface: A physicist asks about the smallest changes in a wave's length.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the tides with the least difference between high and low water, occurring at the moon's quarters.

clue.text: English teacher who could make one cross?

parts.note: a lector is a university lecturer, a teacher

explanation.surface: An English teacher wonders who might annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make one cross' looks like angering someone; it means marking an X on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter puts an X on the ballot paper, so a person entitled to vote is one who marks a cross.

clue.text: Old cathedral providing sanctuary for the German Liberal

indicators.note: the cathedral word shelters the other pieces within it

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: An old cathedral gives refuge to a German Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small English city famous for its cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly describes people getting on in years, a gentler synonym for aged.
